can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can see that a Windows node tool failed, but existing telemetry does not explain whether it was rejected by exec policy, blocked before sandbox execution, failed inside the command, timed out, or could not deliver its response. Gateway and local MCP invocations also lack a shared end-to-end diagnostic view.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds provider-neutral, privacy-reviewed instrumentation for gateway and MCP node tool calls without changing either protocol. Typed diagnostics preserve command execution semantics while reporting stable outcomes, failure categories, authorization/run phases, sandbox application and fallback details, and response-delivery failures.

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose why an agent tool failed from traces, metrics, and bounded failure-only logs. `system.run` telemetry distinguishes exec-policy denial, unsupported sandbox requests, MXC availability/fallback, command failure, timeout, and transport failure without exporting command arguments, payloads, output, paths, credentials, or error messages.

## Evidence

- Live collector observation showed the current hierarchy: `openclaw.node.tool.invoke` → `openclaw.node.tool.execute` → `openclaw.node.tool.system_run.authorize` / `openclaw.node.tool.system_run.run`.
- Collector attributes distinguished an exec-policy denial from sandbox precondition denials and reported sandbox requested/applied/provider/technology values.
- Real gateway → Windows node → MXC E2E passed both command execution and tray-data containment proofs.
- Branch-wide Opus/Codex review found no accepted actionable issues.

## Change Type

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature

- [ ] Chore or infrastructure

## Scope

- [ ] Tray or WinUI UX
- [x] Windows node capability
- [x] Local MCP or `winnode`
- [x] Gateway, connection, or pairing
- [ ] Setup or onboarding
- [x] Permissions, privacy, or security
- [x] Tests, CI, or docs

## Validation

- `./build.ps1` — passed
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 2,885 passed, 31 skipped
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 1,750 passed
- `./scripts/validate-mxc-e2e.ps1` — 2 passed; both required gateway MXC proofs completed

## Real Behavior Proof

- Environment tested: Windows ARM64, .NET SDK 10.0.301
- PR head or commit tested: `37b84d86`
- Exact steps or command run: `./scripts/validate-mxc-e2e.ps1`; manual gateway `system.run` invocations with OTLP export enabled
- Evidence after fix: collector displayed end-to-end invoke/execute/authorize/run spans with typed outcome, error category, ingress, and sandbox attributes
- Observed result: exec-policy rejection reported `exec_policy_denied`; sandbox precondition rejection reported `sandbox_denied` with finite sandbox metadata; gateway MXC execution and containment proofs passed
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): N/A
- Not verified or blocked: no durable collector screenshot link is attached; live local MCP invocation proof was not captured separately

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? (`Yes`/`No`): No
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No
- New or changed network calls? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes
- Command or tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No
- If any answer is `Yes`, explain the risk and mitigation: Opt-in OTLP export now includes node-tool operational signals through the existing user-configured endpoint. Attributes are finite and explicitly allowlisted; user content, commands, arguments, output, paths, credentials, and exception messages are excluded.

## Compatibility and Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes
- Config or environment changes? (`Yes`/`No`): No
- Migration needed? (`Yes`/`No`): No
- If yes, list the exact upgrade steps: N/A
